evidence.claim: In his second appearance before the Hamburg inquiry, Scholz denied any influence on the Warburg tax procedure and said he still could not remember the contents of the meetings.
evidence.title: Scholz vor Cum-Ex-Ausschuss: "Habe keinen Einfluss genommen"
evidence.excerpt: In his second appearance before the Hamburg inquiry, Scholz denied any influence on the Warburg tax procedure and said he still could not remember the contents of the meetings.
evidence.source_locator: lead, first two paragraphs, and the section headed "Weiterhin keine Erinnerung"
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Public-broadcaster reporting of a live parliamentary hearing with direct quotations and procedural context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct personal testimony by Scholz about his own conduct and memory.
contrary_evidence: The committee continued because new documents and prior contradictions kept the issue open.

evidence.claim: The Berlin administrative court ordered the Chancellery to provide information about Scholz's personal knowledge from a confidential background conversation in the Cum-Ex matter, in response to a press-access dispute that included an allegation he had lied.
evidence.title: Gericht fordert Scholz zu Auskünften auf: Cum-Ex-Affäre erreicht Kanzleramt
evidence.excerpt: The Berlin administrative court ordered the Chancellery to provide information about Scholz's personal knowledge from a confidential background conversation in the Cum-Ex matter, in response to a press-access dispute that included an allegation he had lied.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Strong contemporaneous reporting of a specific court order and its factual basis.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 legal scrutiny of Scholz's conduct and public-accountability duties
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Scholz's personal knowledge and the Chancellery's response to inquiry.
contrary_evidence: This was a procedural order, not a finding that Scholz lied or acted corruptly.

evidence.claim: In a current-hour debate, all parliamentary groups called for full clarification of the Cum-Ex scandal and several speakers urged Scholz to contribute to the inquiry; the article also notes accusations that he had increasing memory lapses.
evidence.title: Alle Fraktionen für Transparenz und Aufklärung bei Cum-Ex
evidence.excerpt: In a current-hour debate, all parliamentary groups called for full clarification of the Cum-Ex scandal and several speakers urged Scholz to contribute to the inquiry; the article also notes accusations that he had increasing memory lapses.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and the section on new indications in the Cum-Ex case
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary record of floor proceedings and the arguments made there.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 parliamentary scrutiny of Scholz's earlier Hamburg conduct
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Scholz's conduct and his duty to help clarify the affair.
contrary_evidence: SPD and Greens rejected claims of political influence, and the Bundestag record does not itself prove wrongdoing.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on internal nuclear-safety alternatives and command-and-control review is still thin.
Internal cabinet deliberations and precise alternative options around the Ukraine response are not visible.
Most policing and complaint-handling evidence is Länder-level, so direct Scholz attribution remains limited.
Direct evidence of 2022 Scholz-led democratic strengthening is thinner than evidence of institutional baseline and judicial constraint.
Direct chancellor-level evidence on personnel selection, correction after failure, and anti-capture choices remains limited.
Post-enactment delivery quality and longer-run durability of the reforms are not fully shown in the 2022 package.
Direct primary evidence on assets, gifts, family benefit, hidden conflicts, or formal self-dealing is missing.
The record remains allegation-heavy rather than adjudication-heavy on deception and obstruction.
Direct evidence on Scholz's personnel selection, correction of underperformers, and internal discipline is thinner than evidence on program design and rollout.
